title: Researchers document Baja California orcas’ hold-and-ram sunfish sequence
summary: A new study describes two filmed encounters in Mexico’s southern Gulf of California where one orca stabilized a sharp-tail sunfish while another rammed it hard enough to fragment it, but the paper does not prove whether that sequence is a learned local tactic or a one-off interaction.

claims.text: A Frontiers in Ethology paper published on 23 July 2026 describes two orca predation events involving sharp-tail sunfish in the southern Gulf of California, Mexico.

sources.title: Fragmentation of Sharp-Tail Sunfish (Masturus lanceolatus) Caused by High-Impact Ramming Behaviour in Orcas (Orcinus orca)

claims.text: In the first event, on 29 July 2024 near an offshore seamount off San José del Cabo, Baja California Sur, an adult female orca held a sharp-tail sunfish by the clavus while an adult male accelerated into it, causing the tissue to fragment.

claims.text: In the second event, on 7 September 2025 in the channel of Isla Cerralvo, a similar hold-and-ram sequence fragmented a sharp-tail sunfish.
